Elena — thanks and congrats on the close. Attached is a draft MAP that embeds our recommended post-signature activation cadence. Highlights below; the attached spreadsheet (signalwave_map_v1.2.xlsx) contains dates, owners, and acceptance criteria.

Summary (high level):
- Phase 0 — Prep & access (Week 0–1): account provisioning, KMS keys, allowlist, baseline throughput tests. Owner: Priyom.
- Phase 1 — Narrow canary (Week 2): 5% traffic routing to Redwood-hosted endpoint for 10 business days; daily quality checks and latency SLO monitor. Acceptance: no P95 latency regression >20% and error rate <0.5%.
- Phase 2 — Broad canary (Week 3–4): expand to 25% traffic, include KV-cache warmup tests and user-simulated load. Add smoke tests for edge prompts.
- Phase 3 — Full roll (Week 5): staged 3-step ramp to 100% with throttled concurrency growth; final training & handover.

Canary windows: we recommend two 10-business-day windows (narrow then broad). See attached canary-window-checklist.pdf for concrete checks (metric thresholds, payload sampling, runbook triggers).

Rollback triggers (examples):
- Sustained error rate >1% for 30+ minutes
- P95 latency >2x baseline for 3 consecutive measurements
- Key hallucination regressions on golden prompt set (failing quality gate)

Training: Marissa will propose 3 sessions — Admin setup, Prompts & Ops, and Troubleshooting/Runbooks — plus a recorded baseline.

Open items:
1) Confirm blackout windows for SignalWave ops (any days/times to avoid canary).
2) Procurement: target start date for billing (will affect license activation).
3) Network egress expectations (we can provide IP ranges and peering guidance).

I'm copying Priyom for runbook specifics and Marissa for training slots. We'll aim to lock Week 2 as the narrow canary if procurement and network are green.

Cheers,
Markus
Head of Customer Implementation | Redwood Inference

Subject: Canary migration runbook excerpt + sign-off request

Team — attaching the canary migration runbook excerpt and a short checklist (canary-migration-runbook.md). Key operational notes and rollback steps below. We need a formal sign-off from SignalWave before we execute the narrow canary.

Operational notes (excerpt):
- Traffic routing: use header-based routing + token sampling (5% narrow canary) routed to endpoint: https://redwood-api.redwood.ai/signalwave/v1/x1
- Metrics to stream: p50/p95 latency, error rate (5xx), completion-length distribution, golden-prompt pass rate, token-cost-per-request.
- Alerting: Pager duty if error rate >1% sustained for 15 minutes; auto-rollback option requires confirmation from SignalWave ops.

Rollback steps (quick):
1) Abort new routing, revert header rule (2 mins)
2) Redirect traffic to previous endpoint snapshot (auto-complete)
3) Postmortem run (owners: Priyom, SignalWave ops)

Requested sign-offs:
- SignalWave PM (Elena) — agreement on narrow canary start date and rollback triggers
- SignalWave Procurement — PO effective date

If everyone is aligned, we will run the narrow canary starting Mon 02 Apr 2028 (Week 2) to allow the procurement window to close and to avoid the 23 Mar blackout.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachment: canary-migration-runbook.md
